   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Les Harding

I thought I would put pen to
paper (or is it finger to key?)
for my first contribution to
'OUTLET'. Along with many other
avid readers of your mag I would
like to add my praise for a
well-produced and high quality
editorial that appeals to the
majority of people.I particular-
ly like the mix of contributions
from beginners and experts
alike.

It's nice to know that other
people (myself included) get a
lot of enjoyment from computers
without a vast knowledge of
programming or using state of
the art equipment.

It's also comforting to know
that there are some real experts
out there willing to help us
lesser mortals solve those
'tricky'bits that we all come up
against from time to time! KEEP
UP THE GOOD WORK!

          All the best,

           Les Harding





Many thanks,Les. Thanks also for
the article which will appear in
a future issue.
                        - Brian

From D.J. Manly, HERTS.



Dear Sir,

I have a Spectrum 48K and Wafa-
drive, both of which are wearing
out and getting unreliable so -
the time came to upgrade.

I purchased a second-hand Plus 3
but soon found that it does not
utilise the disk drive in 48K
mode. Then I found my favourite
wordprocessor, Spectral Writer,
will not run in 128K mode and
the Plus 3 will not drive my
mono green screen monitor (not
enough power from the allocated
port).

So, I thought, if this is what a
small computer can do with a
disc drive then a PC must be
better. I bought a second-hand
PC with colour. Well, I'm glad I
did not buy a new PC.Most of the
software is horrific to use.Some
- if the user makes a mistake -
just stops with a report code.
Some stops to the BIOS and some
are just indecipherable. BUT,
those that do work and revert to
a main menu,are brilliant. Well,
actually,two programs - out of a
dozen or more. Apart from the
colour monitor and the keyboard,
which is nice compared to an
accessory fitted to my 48K Spec-
trum,I am extremely disappointed
with the PC including this w/p
QUILL which is slow compared to
Spectral Writer.

What's this letter about? Well,
I want to go back to the Plus 3
and sell the PC to some other
boffin that understands MS DOS
and all that goes with it. It's
too heavy for me but I need help
with Plus 3 programs and hard-
ware, especially the Plus 3's
nasty habit of reverting to a
white screen in programming mode
and also with Tasword 2 which I
don't like anyway, Spectral
Writer by Softek is far
superior. Has some clever person
converted this program to run on
a Plus 3 in 128K mode and on
disk? If so, I am prepared to
pay for it.
               Yours sincerely,

                 D.J. Manning

P.S. As you probably guessed,the
main reason that I bought a PC
was for a good w/p but I cannot
do things with the PC that can
be done with the Spectrum -
especially accessing printer
controls and drawing to screen
- all easy on a 48K Speccy, if
sometimes long-winded.

P.P.S. This w/p would not even
reset the printer!

Brian Cavers to D.J. Manly

I symphasise - I felt the same
way about First Word on the ST.
However, I'm sure there must be
good wordprocessors on PC's and
ST's but probably costing `50
upwards (and I mean upwards in
the `200 to `300 price range).
Trouble is, who wants to risk
paying out that kind of money
without a week's trial?

Anyway, I don't think I can help
much with Spectral Writer. We do
have a routine to switch to 48K
mode (ROUTE 48 - OUTLET 31) but
you could not then access the
drive.We've a routine to go back
to 128K but it then re-enters
the BASIC editor and I think it

may not work if Spectral Writer
or your printer had corrupted
the 128K routines in the old
printer buffer area. Has anyone
else done this conversion?

                     - Brian

From:    Kevin Snowdon,
         6,Glebe Terrace
       Dunston, Gateshead,
      TYNE & WEAR, NE11 9NQ

Dear Ron & Brian,

I'd like to add a few comments
to the 'USE OF A MONITOR'
discussion. I wired my old 48K
Spectrum up to give a composite
output as Brian outlined in a
previous OUTLET and this gave a
vastly better picture.

I have now got a Spectrum 128K
(original Sinclair One) and I
was a bit disappointed at the
picture quality it gave on my
MATSUI portable television (it
was crap).

The Television has AUDIO and
VIDEO inputs so I made two leads
up as follows :-

PIN 1 OF THE R.G.B. SOCKET TO
THE CENTRE PIN OF A PHONO PLUG

PIN 2 OF THE R.G.B. SOCKET TO
THE OUTER PART OF THE PHONO PLUG

THIS PHONO PLUG GOES INTO THE
VIDEO INPUT OF THE TELEVISION.

THE AUDIO LEAD WAS MADE UP WITH
A STANDARD SINCLAIR JACK PLUG
AND A PHONO SOCKET :-

CENTRE PIN OF JACK PLUG TO
CENTRE PIN OF PHONO PLUG. OUTER
PART OF JACK PLUG TO OUTER PART
OF PHONO PLUG.

THE JACK PLUG GOES INTO THE MIC
SOCKET AND THE PHONO PLUG IN THE
AUDIO INPUT OF THE TELEVISION.

The method not only gives better
pictures and sound but also
enables you to plug the Spectrum
into the Video Recorder for
Video Titling or even creating
your own Karaoke! The music
required is available from any
music shop including the words
to the songs.

I use the excellent program VAR-
ITYPE from OUTLET 34 to produce
the words to be recorded on
video tape while I use a tape
player to feed the music via the
AUDIO IN to the video recorder.
Now, where do I get singing
lessons???

If anybody uses the Art Program
ANIMATOR 1, you can use any of
the character sets that appear
in OUTLET now and again but
remember that the character
codes are shifted by four places
e.g., ANIMATOR 1 character "A",
ENTER character "="; ANIMATER 1
character "B" ENTER character">"
and so on. [If unsure, enter
PRINT CHR$ (CODE "C" -4) where C
is the character you want to
convert, in BASIC. - BC]

Please feel free to write to me
at the above address about any
of the points in my letter.

          Kevin Snowdon

Thanks, Kevin.    - Brian

From C.J. Edwards, WATFORD

I've recently bought a second-
hand printer -a Seikosha GP100A.
It's supposed to have character
mode - double width character
mode and graphics mode.

At switch-on it's in character
mode and I can LLIST programs
O.K. From here on I'm at a
complete loss.

Perhaps someone, somewhere can
give me a some help or advice
but please make it in "plain"
language as I'm no expert.

          Yours truly,

          C.J. Edwards

Brian Cavers to C.J. Edwards

I have no info on this printer
so I will make some guesses. I
assume that you have no manual
(if you do but can't understand
it then send me a photocopy of
the relevant pages). I also have
to assume that the printer is
not Epson-standard.

To get printers to do other than
print text you need to send some
special codes. To do this on the
SAM you must FIRST enter...

           OPEN #3;"B"

You will now be unable to LLIST
properly and may find LPRINT
does not do linefeeds so...

After sending codes use...

     CLOSE #3 : OPEN #3;"T"

    ...to get back to normal.


Now, assuming you have used the
OPEN #3;"B" first, what codes do
you now send to get graphics,
double-width characters etc.? I
don't know your printer so I'd
experiment with...


10 OPEN #3;"B"
20 FOR N=0 TO 255
25 PRINT AT 10,10;N
30 LPRINT CHR$ N;N
35 PAUSE
40 NEXT N

Keep pressing a key and note
down any results. For example,if
15 is printed on the screen then
code 15 is sent to the printer.
If you can see "15" has been
printed in tiny lettering then
note down - 15 gives condensed
text.

Stand by your printer's on/off
switch while doing this as it
may suddenly start printing
miles of garbage or feeding out
sheet after sheet of paper!

When you get to the end at 255,
alter line 30 to...

 LPRINT CHR$ 27; CHR$ N;N

and run it again.

You could try different values
instead of 27 (27 is a standard
ESC code which often precedes a
second code).

Full graphics is more complex
and it will probably not be
possible for you to suss it all
out by this means but you may at
least get one or two codes.

Otherwise, has anyone else got
this printer and can they help?

                     - Brian

From Alan Rutherford

I've a tip that could be useful
for all types of computers using
edge-connectors. The most common
fault on my Spectrum is locking
up or crashing. Over a period of
years I've found this to be
caused by a dirty edge-connector
in 99% of cases.A cure I've done
to keep the dirt at bay is to
replate the edge connector.

This may sound daft but on the
market there is a liquid for
adding silver to worn silver
plate. This stuff will plate the
solder on the edge-connector
with silver. I have restored a
connector that was worn down to
the bare copper and it has come
up like new.

The benefit is tarnishing does
not happen. At least I have gone
for six months without a single
crash. The resistivity appears
to be a lot less also.

The main snag is that the liquid
is expensive. I purchased mine
from the Bettawear catalogue and
a 150mL bottle was `9.99. They
do a 75mL bottle for about
`6.00. My wife stopped moaning
about the cost when I redid all
the silver-plate. It now looks
like new and even my wife is
impressed with the results. The
address is...

Betterware Ltd.,Fairview Estate,
Kingsbury Road, Curdworth, West
Midlands, B76 9EH.

The code for the product is CODE
01280. A 150mL bottle shoul last
for ages.

        - Alan Rutherford






Many thanks Alan. That sounds an
excellent tip. I too, have often
suffered the dreaded crashes due
to a dirty edge-connector but I
need to ask the loan arranger so
that I can get the hey ho silver
- away with oxidation.
                        - Brian

From:     Miles Kinloch
           Flat 3F3L,
       6 Drummond Street,
       Edinburgh EH8 9TU.



Dear Ron & Brian,

A while ago I wrote in offering
instructions to readers for
converting Wordmaster to work in
128 mode to make use of the
Ramdisk, and was surprised at
the large number of replies I
received. In fact, I still get
requests for this from time to
time, I think from people who
take that Outlet as a back issue
- I had a letter only last week
as a matter of fact.

I thought therefore I'd take
this opportunity to repeat my
offer for the benefit of any
newer readers who haven't seen
my original Outletter. (The
conversion just applies to the
48K version of Wordmaster, as
PCG's 128K version is only for
the +2A and +3.) If anyone would
like the details, just send an
SAE and I'll post them to you.

I have learned from my corres-
pondence with people, the conv-
erted program will not work with
Microdrives and Opus Discovery
due to the memory requirements
of these drives but works fine
with Disciple/+D and tape-only
systems.Please state what system
and printer interface you have
if writing.

Finally, a few people who have
done the conversion have since
reported problems with Typeliner
crashing after pressing BREAK to
abort a printout. This can be
fixed by POKE 24713,195; POKE
24714,81; POKE 24715,250 and
re-saving.

Best wishes, Miles Kinloch


Excellent. Thanks Miles. We do
get quite a few inquiries about
converting programs to work on
other systems.If anyone else has
got ANY program working on some
other set-up why not share the
method through these pages? Not
all users are programmers.
                        - Brian

From: Noel White, NORTHANTS.

Dear Mr. Cavers,

As the trouble with cartridges
is building up I wondered if
something could be included in
'OUTLETTERS' asking for suggest-
ions.

To have to dump existing systems
which are working O.K. and go
for a SAM or a Spectrum +3 (2nd-
hand +3's are being advertised
at around `120)is pretty drastic
and in the case of both these
machines there appear to be a
number of snags in getting them
to accept the functions of the
earlier machines - though in the
SAM there are many improvements.

So, how about the alternative of
fitting a disc drive? I would be
most interested to hear of
anyone who has adapted any of
the commercial disc drives(which
are advertised at `50 or less)
to work with the Spectrum+ or +2
possibly using Interface one.

        Sincerely yours,

           Noel White


Brian Cavers to Noel White


This subject has already been
well-covered in OUTLETTERS (see
in particular my reply to Percy
Ellis in OUTLET 37). I always
recommend getting a Disciple or
+D interface with a drive(s).The
main supplier of +D's is Datel,
Govan Road, Fenton Industrial
Estate, Fenton, Stoke-on-Trent,
ST4 2RS for `129.99 including a
drive or `59.99 without (so you
could buy a cheaper drive else-
where). You MUST state which
Spectrum you have as Datel do
different +D's for each type of
Spectrum. For the +2 you must
also state grey(+2)or black(+2A)
as they differ significantly.

Lots of microdrive software will
run immediately on a Disciple or
+D as they all accept the same
syntax for the most part.

The Disciple is more compatible
with the microdrive as it can be
fitted at the same time as
Interface 1 and you can switch
between them and transfer soft-
ware but I do not know of a
supplier any more. It may be
only second-hand Disciples are
generally on sale now. To trans-
fer microdrive programs to the
+D you will need to save them
one by one to tape and load them
back later.If you have UNITRANS+
(OUTLET 20) and the Sinclair
copier that came with later
microdrives you can do this en
masse.

It is not possible to fit a disc
drive to an Interface 1.

                     - Brian

From: Ian Stokes, CAMBRIDGE

 Many thanks for the outstanding
OUTLET discs this month (words
fail me -best thing since sliced
bread, out of this world).
 I have a +3 and would like to
add a second drive but am rather
cheesed off with 3" discs. So, I
would like to have one for 3.5"
or 5.25" discs. The problem is I
ain't got the foggiest idea what
to get (suggestions? pleeezzz).
Also, is it possible to add two
external drives to my +3 or can
I connect a +128 to the +3 and
access disc drives connected to
that (as well as the one on the
+3) and how many disc drives can
I add to a +128?Can I connect it
all up to my nephew's grey +2?

Brian Cavers to Ian Stokes

You can only add one more drive
DIRECT to your +3 but yes,it can
be a 3.5" or 5.25" if you want.
The bad news is that it will
only format to the standard 173K
with the normal dos. The good
news is we had a megaformat in a
previous OUTLET. The bad news is
that it didn't work properly.The
good news is that we have a new
one in next month that should
format an external 3.5" or 5.25"
disc drive to over 700K!

Where can you get a drive? Any
standard drive (WITH A POWER
SUPPLY) will do so you might try
the adverts in some of the PC
magazines (not Amiga).

I think that a cable is normally
supplied and the drive end is
usually a standard Shugart
connector but the computer end
may be either an edge-connector
type or IDC (I think that's what
they're called). Anyway,you need
the edge-connector type so it
may be wise to ring the supplier
first to ask. However, it is
possible to snap on an edge-
connector (from Maplins?) should
you get the wrong cable.

The alternative method is to get
a +D and drive from DATEL, Govan
Road, Fenton Industrial Estate,
Fenton, Stoke-on-Trent, ST4 2RS.
You must state +3 when ordering
as it comes with a "Fixit" that
enables it to work on a +3.

The +D is `59.99 or `129.99 with
one 3.5" drive. Now you could
have a +D attached (to the edge-
connector) with TWO external
drives (although DATEL don't
advertise other than one drive
you could get one or both else-
where).

HOWEVER, although you can still
use the menu loader to load and
run programs from the internal
3" drive (and even a FOURTH
drive connected to the "B" drive
port if you used something like
CATLOADER (OUTLET 33) to change
drives without entering BASIC),
if you SHOULD enter BASIC then
the machine resets to 48K mode
so you cannot then use the 3"
internal drive or the B drive.

The drive(s) attached via the +D
would still work though but you
would have to reset to get back
to the other drives and to use
128K BASIC at all you would have
to switch off and unplug the +D.

Likewise, you can add two drives
to your 128K+ if you get a +D
but you may not be able to use
the same +D on both 128K and +3.
(Ring DATEL on 0782 744324 as it
may work if the Fixit is off).
The same applies to the +2. You
must tell Datel which type of +D
you want when ordering.

A recent DRIVECHAT discussed
drive-SHARING between computers
but I'm not sure I'd recommend
it to someone without technical
know-how.               - Brian.

Brian Cavers to Raymond Hoy

Thanks, Raymond.

Yes,Dave Hood of Betterbytes has
advertised his ORGANISER in our
own OUTBOARD for a long time now
but if anyone has any of the
other BETTERBYTES programs:
DISC MANAGER, DISC MATE, UTILITY

Remember, any articles sent to

                        - Brian

From Kevin Cooper

Hiya!

The screens in OUTLET, can I use
them in my own p.d. programs or
do I need permission from you
(something the SCPDSA said).
Could you please tell me.

Also, the letter I sent in last
time, you asked if I was inter-
ested in how you do the text
files. Could you please tell me?

             Yours,

               KC


Brian Cavers to Kevin Cooper

You don't say which screens you
mean but I assume you mean the
ones in DEMOPIX? If so, yes,they
are public domain - what we call
FREEWARE. Only items marked
FREEWARE are public domain in
OUTLET. Unfortunately, for some
reason, this never got put on to
the DEMOPIX program -it just got
overlooked I guess! I'll try to
remember to add it in future.

As for decompressing our special
compressed text files back into
ordinary text files, I've just
tried my method on both SAM(with
MASTERDOS) and Disciple and it
does not work with them!They are
restricted to streams 4 to 15.

You see, I've only ever used it
on microdrive which has no such
restrictions. The method was to
open an "opentype" file using
stream 2 or 3 and so divert
PRINT or LPRINT to send the text
to a file on disc. I can find no
easy way to do this except with
my (t)rusty microdrive!

I suppose it should be possible
to POKE the code to divert it to
another stream but I'm starting
to wonder why you want to get at
our text files. They are not
public domain - they are our, or
the author's, copyright. Can you
clarify exactly what you want to
do?
                        - Brian

To get printers to do other than print text you need to send some special codes. To do this on the SAM you must FIRST enter...

OPEN #3;"B"

You will now be unable to LLIST properly and may find LPRINT does not do linefeeds so...

After sending codes use...

CLOSE #3 : OPEN #3;"T"

...to get back to normal.

Now, assuming you have used the OPEN #3;"B" first, what codes do you now send to get graphics, double-width characters etc.? I don't know your printer so I'd experiment with...

10 OPEN #3;"B" 20 FOR N=0 TO 255 25 PRINT AT 10,10;N 30 LPRINT CHR$ N;N 35 PAUSE 40 NEXT N

Keep pressing a key and note down any results. For example,if 15 is printed on the screen then code 15 is sent to the printer. If you can see "15" has been printed in tiny lettering then note down - 15 gives condensed text.

Stand by your printer's on/off switch while doing this as it may suddenly start printing miles of garbage or feeding out sheet after sheet of paper!

When you get to the end at 255, alter line 30 to...

LPRINT CHR$ 27; CHR$ N;N

and run it again.

You could try different values instead of 27 (27 is a standard ESC code which often precedes a second code).

           OPEN #3;"B"

Теперь вы не сможете нормально делать LLIST,
и может оказаться, что LPRINT не переводит
строку, поэтому...

После отправки кодов используйте...

     CLOSE #3 : OPEN #3;"T"

    состояние.

чтобы получить графику, символы двойной
ширины и т.д.? Я не знаю ваш принтер, так
что я бы поэкспериментировал с...

```text
10 OPEN #3;"B"
20 FOR N=0 TO 255
25 PRINT AT 10,10;N
30 LPRINT CHR$ N;N
35 PAUSE
40 NEXT N
```

Продолжайте нажимать клавишу и записывайте
результаты. Например, если на экране
напечатано «15», значит, код 15 был
отправлен на принтер. Если вы видите, что
